Finland’s Valtatec Unveils New Eco-Efficient Hydraulic Press for Machinery Sector

HELSINKI, June 13 — Finnish machinery manufacturer Valtatec unveiled its latest hydraulic press on Thursday, aiming to boost energy efficiency and productivity for heavy industry clients in the region.

The new model, called the VT-Force 5000, was introduced at a launch event at Valtatec’s headquarters in Tampere. According to the company, the press features an advanced energy recovery system and intelligent automation controls designed to reduce power consumption by up to 18 percent compared to previous models.

“Our clients are demanding more sustainable solutions, and the VT-Force 5000 is our answer,” said Mikko Laaksonen, Valtatec’s chief executive officer. “We believe this press sets a new standard for efficiency in European heavy machinery.”

The machinery sector is a cornerstone of Finland’s export-driven economy, with the industry employing more than 100,000 people nationwide, according to the Finnish Engineering Industries Federation. Demand for energy-efficient equipment has grown in recent years amid tightening EU regulations and rising electricity costs.

“Finnish manufacturers are under increasing pressure to cut emissions and improve energy use,” said Hanna Miettinen, a senior analyst at Nordic Industrial Research. “Innovations like Valtatec’s new press will help local firms stay competitive.”

Valtatec said the VT-Force 5000 can be integrated into existing assembly lines and is equipped with a digital monitoring system that enables predictive maintenance and remote diagnostics. The company expects to begin deliveries to domestic customers in August, with initial shipments to Germany and Sweden planned for the fourth quarter.

Jari Koskinen, chair of the Finnish Metalworkers’ Union, welcomed the launch. “Investments in new technology are vital for keeping manufacturing jobs in Finland,” he said.

Valtatec did not disclose pricing for the new model but said it expects “strong interest” from both large-scale manufacturers and mid-sized firms across the Nordic region.

The launch comes as industry groups report a steady recovery in machinery orders following last year’s slowdown, with export demand showing particular strength in the first half of 2024.
